tasks.short: Direct financial performance, funding priorities and corrective action.

steps.what: Assemble actuals, cash balances and forecasts for financial review.
Read the financial pack and identify questions requiring executive attention.

loop.input: Reconciled financial performance pack, management explanations and previous decision record.
loop.output: Source-linked variance explanations and proposed financial review questions.
loop.check: Validate every figure against the pack; distinguish management explanations from inferred causes.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per pack; unsupported explanations become questions for finance.
loop.why_not_simpler: Thresholds find numerical changes; reading management explanations and framing questions needs language interpretation.

steps.what: Challenge assumptions and negotiate funding trade-offs with executives.
Choose allocations and corrective actions within delegated authority.
Update approved allocations and financial controls.
Chase action updates and prepare unresolved items for the next review.

tasks.design: Configure a reconciled financial dashboard in the {BI}, drawing actuals from the {ERP}, cash from the {BANK} and approved forecasts from the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded model drafts source-linked review questions; approved allocation changes pass through the {WORKFLOW}, while the {PROJECT} tracks actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent account mappings, separate cash data and informal action tracking made recurring preparation expensive. Funding choices still depended on executive judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and configurable dashboards cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building missing mappings, checks and small drafting loops.
tasks.still_hard: Forecast uncertainty, investment trade-offs and disputes over scarce funds remain executive work. Reliable financial definitions and delegated authority must be agreed before writes are enabled.
tasks.human_edge: The chief executive accepts risk, negotiates competing priorities and explains why one investment takes precedence.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less pack preparation and action chasing, with more time for funding trade-offs. No formal decision rights change; the chief executive can exercise existing delegated allocation authority more frequently.

reach.task: Translate a spending reduction into a feasible operational capacity plan.
reach.learn: Capacity constraints, service commitments and how operational changes affect cash.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI summarises reports and answers data questions; data-model quality remains a constraint.
Board's FP&A Agent drafts narratives about financial assumptions and risks.
The digest reports a vendor case of Fivetran saving 12 hours monthly on executive reporting; its method is not given.
Step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.

assumptions: The baseline is a mid-size European company with a finance team and recurring executive financial reviews.
Time shares cover the task across participating roles, not just the chief executive's personal time.
Existing reporting and approval features can handle standard cases after configuration.
Build ranges cover one financial review process and exclude major ledger remediation.
Preparation can be offered as a personal read-only workspace using authorised exports; shared writes require company access.
GDPR applies to personal data; the proposed dashboard uses aggregate financial measures.
unknowns: Available reporting features, connectors and permitted financial data access.
Current reconciliation quality and account mappings.
Which allocations require board approval and which fall within executive authority.
Whether proposed controls affect employees and require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration produce the required pack without custom integration?
Which variance questions change an executive funding decision?
Can allocation updates be validated and reversed through existing approval controls?
new_work: Investigate failed reconciliations and stale financial feeds.
Maintain financial mappings, alert thresholds and delegation rules.
Review queued allocation changes before they take effect.

tasks.short: Discuss issues with board members and staff, resolve disagreements and coordinate action.

steps.what: Arrange the discussion and request agenda items.
Read agenda papers and identify unresolved issues.

loop.input: Authorised agenda papers and previous decision record.
loop.output: Source-linked meeting brief with unresolved questions and conflicting statements.
loop.check: Require source locations for factual claims; flag missing papers and conflicting accounts.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per agenda; unreadable or unsupported material goes to the paper owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template organises papers but cannot summarise their free-text arguments or identify conflicting accounts.

steps.what: Explore concerns, hear competing views and work towards agreement.
Confirm the resolution, accountable owners and any required escalation.
Write minutes recording decisions, dissent and action assignments.

loop.input: Secretary's meeting notes, explicit resolution and action assignments.
loop.output: Draft minutes with decisions, dissent, owners and deadlines.
loop.check: Match each decision to explicit notes; mark ambiguous ownership and deadlines as unresolved.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; the secretary resolves ambiguity with participants.
loop.why_not_simpler: Meeting notes vary in language and structure; extracting decisions requires contextual reading.

steps.what: Enter agreed actions and request progress updates.

tasks.design: Use the {CALENDAR} and {WORKFLOW} to collect agenda items and arrange internal discussions. Bounded drafting loops prepare briefs and minutes from authorised material in the {DOCS}; chair-approved actions feed the {PROJECT} for reminders and progress tracking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation and follow-up crossed calendars, papers and informal notes. The central work depended on trust, persuasion and context that software could not replace.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and action tracking cover routine coordination. Bounded text drafting can shorten preparation and minute writing without automating the discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Private concerns, political judgement, unresolved disagreement and accurate treatment of dissent remain difficult. Confidential papers need separate access boundaries and retention settings under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: The chief executive reads the room, earns trust and makes commitments that participants believe.
tasks.altitude: The week has less agenda preparation and follow-up administration, while substantial discussion time remains. No decision rights change.

reach.task: Turn an executive resolution into a delivery plan across departments.
reach.learn: Operational dependencies, escalation routes and realistic ownership of actions.

evidence.claim: Board Intelligence Report Writer drafts structured papers from management documents, supporting preparation rather than replacing deliberation.
The UK cross-government trial reported drafting time savings, but these were self-reported and human oversight remained required.
Scheduling, action tracking and the proposed minutes workflow are feasible patterns; the digest gives no measured chief-executive meeting outcome.

assumptions: Most task time is human discussion, consistent with the supplied priors.
Time shares cover the task across participating roles.
The baseline includes a secretary or assistant for formal discussions; informal discussions may omit minutes.
Drafting uses written notes and does not require meeting recording.
A personal brief can use authorised papers without company-wide integration.
Access estimates include confidentiality review and any employee consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Who may access board papers, staff concerns and meeting notes.
Which meetings require formal minutes and chair approval.
Whether participants currently record meetings and what retention policy applies.
Whether existing scheduling and action tracking features are available.
research_questions: Which preparation steps reduce repeated discussion of unresolved issues?
Can briefs and minutes work from written notes alone?
Which action fields must be explicit before automatic entry is reliable?
new_work: Check briefs for omissions and misleading summaries.
Review minutes for decisions, dissent and confidentiality.
Resolve unclear action owners and deadlines.
Maintain access groups, agenda templates and reminder settings.

tasks.short: Prepare and secure approval for operating and programme budgets.

steps.what: Retrieve actual spending, commitments and staffing costs to establish the budget baseline.
Submit departmental spending proposals and explain their assumptions.
Consolidate submissions and calculate scenarios against funding limits.
Challenge requests and choose a proposed budget with executive colleagues.
Prepare the budget approval paper explaining choices, assumptions and risks.

loop.input: Validated proposed budget, agreed assumptions and scenario comparisons.
loop.output: Draft approval paper with linked figures, assumptions and unresolved risks.
loop.check: Generate tables deterministically; validate every cited figure and prohibit unsupported risk explanations.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per version; unresolved claims return to the finance team.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables and calculations are deterministic; explaining negotiated assumptions requires bounded language drafting.

steps.what: Review the proposed budget and approve it or request changes.
Load the approved budget and release spending limits.

tasks.design: Configure budget forms, versions and scenario calculations in the {WORKFLOW}, with validated baselines from the {ERP} and aggregate staffing costs from the {HCM}. A bounded loop drafts the approval paper in the {DOCS}; after board approval and finance validation, a deterministic integration loads the approved version into the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departments used different assumptions and versions, while finance merged submissions and explained changes manually. Planning configuration and integrations competed with other finance priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable forms and calculation engines already cover collection and consolidation. AI-assisted coding makes small validation and integration components cheaper to build, while bounded drafting handles the narrative.
tasks.still_hard: Demand estimates, staffing choices and funding trade-offs remain uncertain. Cleaning cost-centre mappings and agreeing common planning assumptions may take longer than building the workflow.
tasks.human_edge: Executives judge which commitments are credible and defend the consequences of funding choices.
tasks.altitude: Finance spends less time merging versions, and the chief executive can revisit programme funding between annual budgets. Board approval rights and spending mandates stay unchanged.

reach.task: Build the operational demand and capacity assumptions behind a programme budget.
reach.learn: Unit costs, demand drivers, staffing lead times and sensitivity analysis.

evidence.claim: Pigment supports anomaly detection, report creation and financial model building.
Board's FP&A Agent writes narratives about assumptions and risks.
Board Intelligence reports Apex Group recovering 60% of report preparation time; this is a vendor case, not a budget-wide estimate.
Deterministic consolidation, controlled budget loading and the effort ranges are design estimates.

assumptions: Departments currently submit budget workbooks, while actuals remain in the {ERP}.
Time shares cover participating roles across one budget preparation cycle.
The board approves the company budget; smaller programme approvals may be delegated.
Scenario calculations use explicit financial formulas rather than model-generated arithmetic.
The initial release uses aggregate staffing costs and does not recommend individual employment decisions.
A personal version can validate authorised budget exports; shared submissions and loading require company access.
Access ranges include GDPR review and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Existing planning features, licences and import interfaces.
Number of entities, currencies, cost centres and budget owners.
Quality of staffing cost totals and purchase commitments.
Approval thresholds and required consultation for proposed staffing changes.
research_questions: Can existing planning configuration replace workbook consolidation?
Which assumptions must be shared across departments for scenarios to be comparable?
Can an approved budget version be locked, reconciled and loaded without manual rekeying?
new_work: Resolve invalid submissions and mapping exceptions.
Maintain planning formulas, submission forms and scenario assumptions.
Review narrative claims and unresolved risks.
Reconcile approved totals against the active budget after loading.

tasks.short: Set organizational direction, approve policies and coordinate their implementation.

steps.what: Collect performance reports, risks and proposals for an executive direction review.
Assess the pack and identify strategic tensions and missing evidence.

loop.input: Authorised direction review pack, stated priorities and previous decisions.
loop.output: Source-linked questions about conflicting objectives, missing evidence and changed assumptions.
loop.check: Link each question to supplied evidence; label interpretations and preserve contrary evidence.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per review; unresolved contradictions go to the responsible executive.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules flag missed targets, but comparing free-text proposals and their assumptions needs contextual reading.

steps.what: Debate strategic options, operational constraints and stakeholder consequences.
Choose objectives, policy direction and accountable executive sponsors.
Translate the agreed direction into a policy draft and implementation brief.

loop.input: Approved direction, existing policies and requirements supplied by responsible specialists.
loop.output: Policy draft and implementation brief with a change list and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Trace each substantive change to the decision or a supplied requirement; flag conflicting clauses.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved legal or operational questions return to specialists.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but reconciling existing policy language with new direction requires contextual drafting.

steps.what: Approve the policy after required specialist review and consultation.
Publish approved policy and assign implementation milestones.
Collect milestone progress and outcome measures for executive review.

tasks.design: Configure a direction review pack from approved material in the {DOCS} and outcome measures in the {BI}. Bounded loops draft review questions and policy changes, while executives make the choices and approve publication after required consultation. The {WORKFLOW} publishes approved versions and creates milestones in the {PROJECT}, whose progress feeds the next review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Strategic evidence, policy versions and delivery updates were maintained separately. The core choices involved competing values and uncertain consequences rather than stable rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned records and configurable workflows can connect approval to implementation. Small drafting loops can compare supplied documents, while AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting existing data.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing direction, changing behaviour and judging unintended consequences remain human work. GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; employee monitoring or allocation systems need separate assessment, and consultation duties depend on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The chief executive chooses which outcomes matter, builds support and accepts responsibility when policy has difficult consequences.

ambition.what: Monthly stop-or-adjust review of one strategic initiative

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting status and rewriting policy to testing assumptions with delivery owners. No formal authority expands; existing authority to pause or redirect initiatives becomes easier to exercise with current evidence.

reach.task: Pilot an approved policy change and assess its operational effects.
reach.learn: Pilot design, adoption barriers, outcome measures and when to recommend stopping.

evidence.claim: Board Intelligence Report Writer drafts structured management papers and flags missing forward-looking analysis.
Copilot in Power BI supports report summaries and data questions, conditional on suitable underlying data.
The AI Act identifies certain staff performance monitoring and task allocation uses as high-risk.
The documented flawed report contained fabricated references, supporting explicit source checks for drafted policy material.
The proposed workflow, time shares and build ranges are planning estimates rather than documented strategy outcomes.

assumptions: The baseline is an executive-led policy or operational change within a mid-size European company.
Time shares cover participating roles and exclude substantive delivery of the resulting initiative.
Existing reporting provides aggregate operational measures rather than individual performance scoring.
The first release covers one policy family and one implementation process.
A personal preparation workspace can start with authorised documents; publishing and assignment require shared access.
Consent and access estimates include relevant employee consultation; major negotiations may exceed the range.
unknowns: Which strategic and policy decisions are reserved for the board.
Applicable national consultation requirements and employee representative arrangements.
Whether existing policies conflict or lack clear ownership.
Availability and reliability of operational outcome measures.
Whether any proposed initiative involves high-risk AI uses or significant personal-data processing.
research_questions: Which outcome measure would justify stopping or changing the selected initiative?
Can policy approval, version control and publication use existing configuration?
How can review packs preserve dissent and uncertainty alongside headline performance?
What evidence can distinguish implementation activity from actual operational improvement?
new_work: Check drafted questions and policy changes against their sources.
Maintain policy versions, permissions and approval routes.
Coordinate required specialist review and employee consultation.
Investigate missing progress data and misleading outcome measures.
Review whether implemented changes produced their intended effects.

role.altitude: The chief executive spends less time assembling evidence, merging budgets and chasing actions. More time goes to investment choices, difficult conversations and testing strategic assumptions; board powers and executive mandates remain unchanged.
reach: General and operations manager: connect executive funding choices to operational capacity and service commitments.
General and operations manager: pilot policy changes and report whether outcomes justify continuing.
skills_to_grow: Read financial scenarios and challenge their assumptions.
Distinguish reported facts, interpretations and unresolved uncertainty.
Design operational measures that support stop-or-adjust decisions.
Set clear delegation limits and action-level approval rules.
Facilitate disagreement and negotiate credible commitments.
role.ambitious_version: Run a shorter management cycle: review discretionary investment weekly, reforecast programme funding quarterly and make a monthly stop-or-adjust decision on one strategic initiative.
